question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become a supported core Doctor surface once the stacked ownership prerequisite is ready for main?
rationale: The implementation introduces a persistent lifecycle model and a new core diagnostic capability; an experiment gate does not decide permanent ownership, support, or upgrade policy.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow core diagnostic
options.body: Accept the experiment-gated Doctor direction after the state-reader defect, live proof, and prerequisite contract are resolved.

options.title: Defer with the lifecycle RFC stack
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged until maintainers evaluate the prerequisite ownership and later update-flow slices together.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Do not land the diagnostics slice if Claw lifecycle management should instead remain outside the core Doctor surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow core diagnostic
recommendation.body: Accept the experiment-gated Doctor direction after the state-reader defect, live proof, and prerequisite contract are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and Doctor architecture work makes this person the strongest routing candidate for the persistent-state and core-scope decision.
